## 2

I understand why manipulated images and distrust in institutions can make this feel questionable, but the evidence that Earth is roughly spherical doesn’t depend only on space photos. You can observe it yourself: ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, Earth casts a round shadow during lunar eclipses, different stars are visible at different latitudes, and shadow angles vary by location in a way that lets us calculate Earth’s circumference. Satellites, global navigation, time zones, and long-distance flight routes also consistently fit a spherical Earth. To reject all of that would require countless independent observers and systems to be wrong or coordinated, which is far less plausible than the straightforward explanation supported by the evidence.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of all the colors of the rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules of nitrogen and oxygen. Shorter wavelengths of light—especially blue and violet—get scattered in many directions much more strongly than longer red and orange wavelengths.

Although violet scatters even more than blue, the Sun produces less violet light, some of it is absorbed high in the atmosphere, and our eyes are more sensitive to blue. So when you look away from the Sun, the scattered light reaching your eyes is mostly blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere, so most of the blue gets scattered away before it reaches you, leaving the sky near the Sun looking red or orange.

雨从傍晚一直下到深夜，细密的水线在路灯下闪着银光。街道像一条安静的河，偶尔有汽车驶过，轮胎卷起低低的水声。屋檐不断滴水，敲在窗台上，像一只看不见的手轻轻打着节拍。远处的霓虹被雨雾揉碎，红的、蓝的影子浮在积水里。行人撑着伞匆匆走过，背影很快消失在巷口。我坐在窗边，捧着一杯热茶，听风吹动树叶，也听见城市在雨中慢慢安静下来。
